item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=predictive+information+dissipation+thermodynamics+information+engines+bounds&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.53846/goediss-4985\", \"title\": [\"Foundations of Stochastic Thermodynamics\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.53846/goediss-4985\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.20944/preprints202610.0946.v1\", \"title\": [\"Physical Cost of Observer-Information Entropy Production: From Stochastic Thermodynamics to Fisher–Shannon Information  Dissipation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Observer-information entropy production quantifies the loss of recoverable information about a physical source when an already formed observation undergoes source-independent irreversible degradation. The statistical second-law statement \\\\[ \\\\Sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}}[s,t] =I(X;R_s)-I(X;R_t) =I(X;R_s\\\\mid R_t)\\\\ge 0 \\\\] follows from data processing, but by itself it does not identify a physical energetic or thermodynamic cost. This paper establishes such a connection within an explicit and deliberately restricted stochastic-thermodynamic regime. We consider a finite observer memory $R_t$ coupled to a single heat bath at temperature $T$. A source label $X$ is fixed during the passive relaxation, the transition generator of $R_t$ is independent of $X$, and the memory dynamics satisfies detailed balance with respect to a strictly positive equilibrium law $q$. For the joint source--memory ensemble and for the unconditioned memory marginal, we define the standard stochastic-thermodynamic entropy-production rates. Using the relative-entropy chain rule and the detailed-balance $H$-theorem, we prove the exact correlation-dissipation decomposition \\\\[ \\\\frac{\\\\dot S_{\\\\mathrm{tot}}^{XR}}{k_B} = \\\\sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}} + \\\\frac{\\\\dot S_{\\\\mathrm{tot}}^{R}}{k_B}. \\\\] Consequently, \\\\[ \\\\dot S_{\\\\mathrm{tot}}^{XR}\\\\ge k_B\\\\sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}}, \\\\qquad \\\\Delta S_{\\\\mathrm{tot}}^{XR}[s,t]\\\\ge k_B\\\\Sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}}[s,t]. \\\\] At fixed temperature the same result is an excess-free-energy dissipation bound, \\\\[ \\\\Fex_{XR}(s)-\\\\Fex_{XR}(t) \\\\ge k_BT\\\\Sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}}[s,t]. \\\\] Equality holds when the memory marginal remains at equilibrium, in which case al…
